md_name: Marine microbiome sequencing and metadata workflow
md_description: This DAG represents the generation and processing of sequencing data from marine microbiome samples collected across oceanic regions, including water, sediment, and host-associated microbiomes. It includes field sampling, measurement of environmental conditions, nucleic acid extraction, sequencing library preparation, sequencing capture, and computational processing into community profiles and functional annotations. The workflow also produces an integrated metadata table linking samples to temperature, salinity, depth, collection context, and laboratory methods for downstream ecological analysis.

marine_sampling_sites.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the marine sampling sites themselves: where the sites are located, how they are geographically identified, and what marine region/category they belong to. I excluded field sampling details, environmental measurements, extraction, sequencing, and any derived analytics because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers or experiment identifiers, since those are reserved for the root entity and already-generated fields must not be duplicated.

md_schema.descr: Human-readable name of the oceanic sampling location or station, e.g. 'Station A3' or 'North Pacific subtropical gyre site'. Use the name recorded at the time of sample collection.

Unique identifier for the sampling site or station, formatted as a string such as 'SITE_001' or an expedition-specific station code. This identifies the oceanic region/location where samples were obtained.
Broad marine region in which the sampling site is located, recorded as a categorical geographic origin of the site rather than a measurement. Use the region assigned by the expedition metadata.

Geographic latitude of the sampling site in decimal degrees, measured or assigned for the collection location. Typical range is -90 to 90; positive values indicate north and negative values indicate south.

Geographic longitude of the sampling site in decimal degrees, measured or assigned for the collection location. Typical range is -180 to 180; positive values indicate east and negative values indicate west.

Free-text description of the local collection place at the sampling site, such as reef, transect, harbor, offshore station, or sediment core location. Record the field description used to distinguish sites within the expedition.

Water column or seabed depth associated with the sampling site, in meters, as a site/origin attribute for where the sample was obtained. Typical range is 0 to several thousand meters depending on expedition context.
Categorical description of the habitat context of the sampling site, indicating the broad environmental setting from which the sample originates.

collected_water_sediment_and_host_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the collected samples: what sample type it is, what matrix it came from, the host association where relevant, and basic collection identity. I excluded collection procedure details, preservation method, environmental measurements, extraction, sequencing, and downstream analysis because those belong to Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided any sample identifier field that would duplicate root-level identifiers or already-generated fields.

md_schema.descr: Human-readable name assigned to the collected sample at the time of field collection, e.g. 'surface_water_01' or 'sediment_core_B2'. Use the expedition's sample label as recorded in the field.
Unique string identifier for the collected sample, formatted as an expedition or laboratory code such as 'SAMP_0001'. This identifies one physical field-collected microbiome sample.
Primary physical matrix of the collected sample, describing the material from which microbial DNA/RNA was obtained.
Scientific or common name of the marine organism when the sample is host-associated, e.g. 'coral', 'fish', 'sea sponge'. Leave empty or null for non-host-associated environmental samples.
Whether the collected sample is free-living environmental material or associated with a marine host organism.
Replicate number assigned to repeated collections from the same site and sample matrix, typically starting at 1 and increasing for technical or field replicates collected alongside the main sample.

Physical form in which the sample was stored after field collection and before downstream processing, such as frozen whole sample, preserved pellet, or fixed tissue. This is an intrinsic sample attribute describing its collected state.

field_sampling_and_preservation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included operational fields describing how field collection and preservation were performed: collection timing, preservation method, holding conditions, and the responsible field workflow. I excluded sample identity, site origin, environmental measurements, and any properties of the resulting samples because those belong to Entity, Capture, or downstream nodes. I also avoided fields that would describe the output sample itself beyond a minimal process quality indicator, and I did not repeat any identifier-style fields already generated for sample entities.

md_schema.descr: Date on which the marine sample was collected in the field, recorded at the time of sampling in local or expedition standard date format. Use this to link collection to downstream environmental and laboratory records.
Field collection method used to obtain the sample, such as grab sampling, filtration, core extraction, or swabbing. Record the operational method applied at the site.
Method used immediately after collection to preserve the sample for downstream molecular analysis, recorded as the field-preservation procedure applied on site.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the sample was held during preservation or transport after collection, measured or set in the field workflow. Typical values may range from below 0 for frozen storage to about 4 for chilled transport.
Elapsed time in minutes between collection of the sample and initiation of preservation, measured for each field sample to capture handling delay. Typical values are 0 to several tens of minutes.
Number of researchers or field staff directly involved in the sampling and preservation step for the sample collection event.
Simple quality/status indicator for whether the field-preserved sample met the intended handling conditions for downstream molecular analysis, assessed after collection and preservation.

environmental_measurement_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included instrument configuration and measurement-session fields specific to the environmental sensor setup used at sampling: the device identity, measurement timing, and the captured environmental parameters themselves. I excluded sample identity, preservation, extraction, sequencing, and raw file properties because those belong to Entity, Process, Signal, or downstream nodes. I also avoided fields that describe the raw environmental records file, since file-format and storage metadata belong on the Signal node produced by this capture.

md_schema.descr: Date and time when the environmental measurements were acquired at the sampling location, recorded at the moment the CTD profiler or field sensors were deployed. Use local expedition time or UTC consistently across the dataset.
Manufacturer of the field instrument used to capture temperature, salinity, and depth, e.g. the CTD profiler vendor. Record the hardware manufacturer responsible for the measurement device.
Model name or number of the field instrument used for environmental measurement capture, such as a CTD package model identifier.
Serial number or other unique hardware identifier for the specific environmental measurement instrument used during the capture session, formatted as a string such as 'SN12345'.
Name or label for the active sensor configuration used during capture, if multiple probes or channels were available on the field instrument.

Depth in meters at which the environmental measurements were recorded, as controlled or reported by the capture session. Typical values range from 0 at the surface to the sampled water or seafloor depth.
In situ temperature in degrees Celsius measured by the field sensors at the sampling location and time. Typical marine values are approximately -2 to 40 depending on region and depth.
Practical salinity units measured at the sampling location and time using the field instrument. Typical marine values are roughly 0 to 40 PSU depending on freshwater influence and ocean region.
Brief operator notes about the measurement session, such as probe equilibration issues, bottle fire timing, or unusual field conditions that affected the environmental capture.

environmental_conditions_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact properties: the file or record format, size, dimensions/shape, basic technical quality, and where the raw environmental readout is stored. I excluded the instrument configuration and measurement settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded scientific interpretation or normalized values because those would be downstream derivative or analysis fields. I also avoided repeating the actual temperature/salinity/depth measurements, since those are capture-side values rather than raw-file metadata for the signal artifact.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw environmental readout file or record set produced by the capture session, e.g. 'ctd_cast_01.csv' or 'station_A3_env.txt'. Use the filename as stored in the data archive.
File format of the raw environmental conditions signal, such as CSV, TXT, TSV, or JSON, representing the stored raw readout from the field capture instrument.
Size of the raw environmental readout file in bytes at the time of ingestion or archiving. Typical values depend on instrument output and may range from kilobytes to megabytes.
Number of raw measurement records or rows contained in the environmental conditions signal file, counted from the raw capture artefact after acquisition.
Number of recorded variables or channels in the raw signal, typically including temperature, salinity, and depth. Use this to capture the dimensionality of the raw artefact.

Technical quality flag for the raw environmental signal, indicating whether the file was complete and readable at ingestion. Assess this on the raw artefact, not the scientific validity of the measurements.
Filesystem or object-store path where the raw environmental conditions signal is archived, recorded as the location of the raw data artefact at rest.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included operational fields describing how nucleic acid extraction was performed: extraction kit/protocol, target molecule type, reagent and input settings, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded sample identity, sample matrix, environmental capture, raw file properties, and downstream nucleic-acid entity properties because those belong to Entity, Capture, Signal, or the extracted-nucleic-acids node. I also avoided fields that would describe the purified nucleic acids themselves beyond the extraction method and yield-related process context, since output material properties belong on the output Entity node.

md_schema.descr: Date on which nucleic acid extraction was performed for the marine sample, recorded at the start or completion of the laboratory extraction workflow.
Name of the extraction protocol or kit used to purify nucleic acids from the collected sample, e.g. a commercial kit or lab-developed protocol name.
Primary nucleic acid type targeted by the extraction workflow, describing whether DNA, RNA, or both were intended to be purified from the sample.

Mass of the starting sample material used for extraction, in milligrams, measured or recorded at the beginning of the extraction workflow. Typical values depend on sample type and may range from sub-milligram to grams for bulk material.
Lot number or batch identifier for the extraction reagents or kit used in the process, recorded to support reproducibility and traceability.
Volume of elution buffer used to recover purified nucleic acids at the end of the extraction, in microliters. Typical values are often 20 to 100 µL depending on the protocol.
Process-level indicator of whether the extraction produced usable nucleic acids for downstream library preparation, assessed after purification and before handoff to the next step.

extracted_nucleic_acids.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the purified nucleic-acid material itself: molecule type, concentration, purity, integrity, and storage status. I excluded extraction protocol details, reagent lots, and other process parameters because those belong to the upstream extraction Process node, and I excluded library preparation or sequencing attributes because those belong downstream. I also avoided any sample-origin identifiers already represented elsewhere and kept the fields focused on what the extracted nucleic acids are rather than how they were made.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified nucleic-acid aliquot, formatted as an inventory or laboratory code such as 'NA_0001'. This identifies the extracted DNA/RNA material derived from a marine sample.
Type of purified nucleic acid present in the aliquot, describing the material after extraction.

Measured concentration of the purified nucleic acids in nanograms per microliter, typically determined after extraction and before library preparation. Typical values may range from below 1 to hundreds of ng/µL depending on sample yield.
Total mass of purified nucleic acids recovered from the extraction, in nanograms, measured for the extracted aliquot prior to downstream processing.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 of the extracted nucleic acid material, measured after purification to assess protein contamination. Typical DNA values are often around 1.8 and RNA values around 2.0.
Quality metric describing nucleic-acid integrity, such as RIN, DIN, or a lab-specific integrity score, recorded for the extracted material before library preparation.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the purified nucleic acids prior to downstream library preparation, recorded for the extracted material. Typical storage values include 4, -20, or -80.
Volume of the purified nucleic-acid aliquot available for downstream use, in microliters, measured after extraction and aliquoting.

sequencing_library_preparation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included operational fields that describe how extracted nucleic acids were converted into sequencing-ready libraries: library prep kit/protocol, amplification and indexing settings, insert/fragmentation targets, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded properties of the extracted nucleic acids themselves, raw sequence file properties, and downstream library identity/size distributions as standalone material attributes because those belong to the upstream Entity node for extracted nucleic acids or the downstream sequencing library Entity node. I also avoided repeating sample identifiers or capture settings from earlier nodes.

md_schema.descr: Date on which sequencing library preparation was performed for the extracted nucleic acids, recorded at the start or completion of the library construction workflow.
Name of the library preparation protocol or commercial kit used to convert extracted nucleic acids into sequencing-ready libraries, e.g. a kit name or laboratory protocol label.

Mass of extracted nucleic acid input used to build the sequencing library, in nanograms, measured or recorded at the start of library preparation. Typical values depend on assay type and may range from sub-nanogram to hundreds of nanograms.

Number of PCR amplification cycles applied during library preparation, recorded as a process parameter when amplification was used. Typical values are often 0 to 20 cycles depending on input material.
Indexing or barcoding strategy used to label libraries for multiplex sequencing, describing how sample-specific indices were added during preparation.
Target library insert size in base pairs, specified during fragmentation or size-selection steps of library preparation. Typical values vary by assay and platform, often from about 200 to 600 bp.
Process-level indicator of whether the library preparation produced a sequencing-ready library meeting expected quality and concentration criteria, assessed after construction and before sequencing.

sequencing_libraries.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included intrinsic properties of the prepared sequencing library itself: library identity, platform compatibility, insert size, concentration, fragment distribution, and storage status. I excluded library preparation protocol details, PCR cycles, and indexing workflow parameters because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided repeating sample- or extract-level identifiers and kept the fields centered on what the library is as a physical sequencing-ready material.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library, formatted as a laboratory or inventory code such as 'LIB_0001'. This identifies the sequencing-ready library derived from a marine nucleic acid extract.
Sequencing platform or instrument family for which the library is compatible, recorded as a material attribute of the prepared library, e.g. Illumina, PacBio, or Oxford Nanopore.

Measured concentration of the prepared library in nanograms per microliter, determined after library construction and before sequencing. Typical values may range from below 0.1 to tens of ng/µL depending on protocol and input material.

Observed or estimated insert size of the prepared library in base pairs, representing the fragment length after preparation and size selection. Typical values are often approximately 200 to 800 bp for short-read libraries.
Summary of the fragment size distribution of the prepared library, reported as a representative numeric value such as peak or modal insert size in base pairs when assessed after preparation.
Index or barcode sequence associated with the prepared library, used to multiplex samples during sequencing. Record the barcode as stored in the library inventory or manifest.
Storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the prepared sequencing library prior to sequencing, recorded after library preparation and before capture. Typical values include 4, -20, or -80.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: I corrected the sequencing_capture schema to avoid collisions with already_generated fields by removing the duplicate hardware-identity field names. I kept only capture-session fields that remain within the sequencing instrument configuration territory and do not repeat earlier metadata. I also avoided downstream raw-file or output attributes, since those belong to the Signal node produced by this capture.

md_schema.descr: Date on which the sequencing run was initiated or completed, recorded for the capture session that produced the raw sequence data.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit used in the run, describing the configured chemistry applied by the instrument during library reading.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured as the expected per-read output length set on the instrument. Typical values depend on platform and assay, often 75 to 300 bp for short-read sequencing.
Indicates whether the sequencing run was configured to produce paired-end reads or single-end reads, as a capture-session setting.
Identifier of the flowcell or chip used for the sequencing run, if applicable to the platform, recorded to track the specific consumable used during capture.
Operator notes describing relevant capture-session details such as run interruptions, loading issues, or instrument alerts observed during sequencing.

raw_sequence_reads.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I kept only raw sequence-file artefact properties and removed the colliding field ids already generated elsewhere in the DAG. Specifically, I excluded read_length_bp and storage_location_path because they were flagged as duplicates, and I avoided instrument, sample, library, and downstream-derived fields. The remaining fields describe the raw FASTQ-like file itself: its name, format, size, read count, basic technical quality, and GC composition.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw sequence read file as stored in the data archive, e.g. 'sample01_R1.fastq.gz' or 'runA_lane2.fastq'. Record the exact file name for the raw FASTQ-like artefact.
File format of the raw sequence data, typically FASTQ or FASTQ-like compressed text files produced by the sequencer. Use the format recorded on disk at ingestion.
Size of the raw sequence read file in bytes at the time of archiving or ingestion. Typical values may range from megabytes to tens of gigabytes depending on sequencing depth.
Number of reads contained in the raw sequence file or file set, counted after sequencing and before any filtering or trimming. This describes the raw signal volume, not the biological sample size.
Average base-call quality score across the raw reads, calculated from the FASTQ quality strings as a technical property of the raw signal. Typical values depend on platform and run quality.
Percent GC content observed across the raw reads, measured as a technical summary of the sequence file contents. Typical values are assay- and taxon-dependent.

read_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included computational workflow parameters describing how raw reads were filtered, trimmed, and denoised: software identity, version, algorithm choices, threshold settings, and a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded raw file properties, upstream sequencing instrument settings, and downstream processed-data file attributes because those belong to the Signal or Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated field ids that collided across DAG steps, especially any generic read-length or storage-location fields, and kept the fields focused on the transformation process itself.

md_schema.descr: Date on which read processing was performed, recorded at the start or completion of the computational filtering and denoising workflow.
Name of the software or pipeline used to process raw reads into analysis-ready sequence data, e.g. a trimmer, denoiser, or integrated bioinformatics workflow.
Version of the processing software or pipeline used for read filtering, trimming, and denoising, recorded to support reproducibility.
Repository URL, package registry location, or source reference for the processing software or pipeline used in read processing. Include the release source used to execute the workflow.
Method or algorithm used to remove sequencing adapters and low-quality tails from raw reads, recorded as the operational trimming approach.
Minimum base quality threshold used during filtering or trimming, expressed as a Phred score. Typical values are often between 10 and 40 depending on pipeline stringency.
Algorithm used to denoise filtered reads into analysis-ready sequence data, such as an exact sequence variant or error-correction method.
Process-level indicator of whether the read processing completed successfully and produced analysis-ready sequence data meeting expected quality criteria.

processed_sequence_data.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result fields for the processed sequence data: the algorithmic product identity, output dimensions, summary technical quality, and representation of the processed sequence set. I excluded raw read file properties, read-processing software parameters, and instrument settings because those belong to the Signal or upstream Process/Capture nodes. I also avoided duplicate generic fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including read-length and storage-location style fields, and kept the schema focused on the analysis-ready output itself.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the analysis-ready processed sequence dataset, formatted as a derivative or analysis code such as 'PROC_0001'. This identifies the denoised and filtered output produced from raw reads.

Name of the computational method or workflow that produced the processed sequence data, recorded as the output-generating algorithmic transformation. This is the method applied to generate the derivative result.

Number of sequence features retained in the processed dataset, such as amplicon sequence variants, operational taxonomic units, or contigs, depending on the analysis pipeline. This is a downstream output dimension measured after processing.

Number of original samples represented in the processed sequence dataset, counted after read processing and before downstream profiling. Use this to capture the size of the derivative result matrix or collection.
Total number of reads retained after filtering, trimming, and denoising in the processed sequence output. This is a computed output metric describing the size of the derivative data.

Minimum abundance or occurrence threshold used to retain features in the processed sequence dataset, expressed as the cutoff applied during output generation. Typical values depend on pipeline design and may be counts or relative abundances.

Summary quality score for the processed sequence dataset, such as retained-read fraction, chimera-free proportion, or a pipeline-specific confidence metric. Record the principal quality indicator reported for the derivative output.
Boolean indicator of whether the processed sequence data are ready for downstream profiling and annotation without additional transformation.

taxonomic_profiling.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included computational profiling parameters that describe how community composition was inferred from processed sequence data: taxonomy reference source, classifier method, confidence thresholds, and output summary settings. I excluded the processed-sequence input properties and the resulting abundance tables because those belong to the upstream Derivative node and the downstream community_taxa_profile Derivative node, respectively. I also avoided previously generated fields such as software identity and generic process dates if they would duplicate earlier process metadata, and focused on the taxonomic inference workflow itself.

md_schema.descr: Date on which taxonomic profiling was performed from the processed sequence data, recorded at the start or completion of the community composition inference step.
Name of the taxonomic reference database used to assign taxa from processed sequences, e.g. SILVA, GTDB, Greengenes, or a project-specific database.
Version or release identifier of the taxonomy reference database used for profiling, recorded to support reproducibility of taxonomic assignments.
Algorithm or classifier used to infer taxonomic composition from processed sequence data, describing the method applied to the derivative input.

Minimum confidence or assignment score required to accept a taxonomic call, expressed as the threshold used during profiling. Typical values may be probabilities between 0 and 1 or percent confidence depending on method.
Taxonomic rank at which the profiling results were summarized, indicating the level of community composition reported by the process.
Process-level indicator of whether taxonomic profiling completed successfully and produced interpretable community composition results.

community_taxa_profile.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only computed-result fields for the taxonomic abundance profile and removed any field ids that collide with earlier DAG steps, including the previously generated sample_count. I retained output identity, abundance scale, diversity and completeness metrics, and matrix sparsity because these describe the derived community profile itself. I excluded upstream process parameters, raw/processed read properties, and any generic counts already used elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the community taxa profile derivative, formatted as an analysis or result code such as 'TAX_0001'. This identifies the computed taxon-abundance output for a marine microbiome sample set.
Unit used to express taxon abundance in the community profile, recorded as the quantitative scale for the derived result. Use the unit reported by the profiling pipeline.

Number of taxonomic features represented in the community profile, such as taxa, amplicon sequence variants aggregated to taxon, or metagenomic taxa assignments. This is the output dimensionality of the derivative table.
Shannon diversity index calculated from the derived taxon abundance profile for each sample or summarized across the profile, recorded as a computed community diversity metric.
Observed taxon richness in the derived community profile, measured as the number of taxa detected in the output abundance table.
Percent of total assigned reads or abundance represented by the retained taxa in the derived profile, used as a summary completeness indicator of the output.
Fraction of zero or absent entries in the community taxa profile matrix, calculated after derivation to describe table sparsity. Typical values are between 0 and 1.

functional_annotation.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included computational annotation parameters that describe how functional potential was inferred from processed sequence data: reference database, annotation method, score thresholds, and summary settings. I excluded processed-sequence inputs and the resulting function-profile outputs because those belong to the upstream Derivative node and the downstream community_function_profile Derivative node, respectively. I also avoided duplicate field ids already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including generic sample-count style fields and any capture/software identifiers that were previously used.

md_schema.descr: Date on which functional annotation was performed from the processed sequence data, recorded at the start or completion of the function inference step.
Name of the functional reference database used to assign genes, orthologs, or pathways from processed sequences, e.g. KEGG, eggNOG, MetaCyc, Pfam, or a project-specific database.
Version or release identifier of the functional reference database used for annotation, recorded to support reproducibility of functional inference.
Algorithm or annotation workflow used to infer functional potential from processed sequence data, describing the computational method applied to the derivative input.
Minimum score or confidence threshold required to accept a functional annotation, expressed in the scale used by the annotation method. Typical values depend on the algorithm and database.
Functional unit or level at which annotation results were summarized, such as gene family, ortholog, enzyme class, or pathway.
Process-level indicator of whether functional annotation completed successfully and produced interpretable functional potential results.

community_function_profile.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result fields describing the functional profile itself: a derivative identifier, output dimensionality, abundance unit, and summary functional coverage/complexity metrics. I excluded annotation database and algorithm settings because those belong to the upstream functional_annotation Process node, and I excluded raw or processed sequence properties because those belong upstream to sequence-related nodes. I also avoided repeating any previously generated generic count or storage fields, keeping the schema focused on the functional abundance/pathway profile as a derived analysis product.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the community function profile derivative, formatted as an analysis or result code such as 'FUN_0001'. This identifies the computed functional abundance or pathway output for a marine microbial community.
Unit used to express functional abundance in the profile, recorded as the quantitative scale for the derived result, such as normalized abundance or relative abundance.
Number of functional features represented in the community function profile, such as genes, orthologs, enzyme classes, modules, or pathways. This is the output dimensionality of the derivative table.
Total number of samples represented in the functional profile output, counted after annotation and profile construction from the processed sequence data.
Percent of pathway or function space covered by the detected features in the derived profile, used as a summary completeness indicator of the output.
Mean abundance of functional features across the derived profile, reported on the same scale as the chosen abundance unit to summarize overall functional signal.
Fraction of zero or absent entries in the functional profile matrix, calculated after derivation to describe table sparsity. Typical values are between 0 and 1.
Diversity index calculated from the derived functional abundance profile, recorded as a computed summary of functional complexity across the marine community.

metadata_table_integration.reasoning: This is a Process node whose semantic territory is the integration workflow that assembles fields from upstream entities, capture signals, and lab methods into one unified analysis table. I included only table-construction parameters and integration-specific quality/output descriptors: the table build date, table schema version, row/column counts, join key strategy, normalization or harmonization choices, provenance coverage, and a process-level completion flag. I excluded the actual sample identifiers, environmental measurements, extraction details, and sequencing details because those are upstream data elements already represented in other nodes and should not be duplicated here. I also avoided output file path or file-format specifics because those belong to the downstream marine_metadata_table derivative rather than the integration process itself.

md_schema.descr: Date on which the metadata integration workflow was executed to assemble the unified marine analysis table.
Version identifier for the integrated metadata table schema used during this integration step, recorded to support reproducibility of the unified table structure.
Strategy used to match and merge records across samples, environmental measurements, and laboratory method sources, such as sample identifier-based joins or composite keys.
Number of rows produced in the unified metadata table after integration, counted at the end of the process. This reflects the number of integrated sample records.
Number of metadata columns present in the unified table after integration, counted after merging upstream fields into the analysis-ready table.
Fraction of table cells left missing or unresolved after integration, calculated as a process-quality indicator for the merged metadata table. Typical values are between 0 and 1.
Method used to standardize upstream field names, units, and categorical values before merging into the unified analysis table, such as controlled vocabulary mapping or unit normalization.
Boolean indicator of whether the metadata integration workflow completed successfully and produced a unified analysis table ready for downstream use.

marine_metadata_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only properties of the integrated metadata table artifact itself and removed duplicated count-style field ids that were already used elsewhere in the DAG. The remaining fields describe table identity, serialization, coverage/completeness, and quality, which are appropriate for the derivative output. I excluded the actual merged sample metadata values because those belong to the integrated content, not the artifact metadata, and I avoided any previously generated row/column count names to prevent cross-step collisions.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated marine metadata table, formatted as a derivative or table code such as 'META_0001'. This identifies the unified table linking samples to location, environmental conditions, and laboratory methods.
Serialization or file format of the integrated metadata table as stored on disk or in an archive, e.g. CSV, TSV, XLSX, or JSON. Record the format of the derivative table artifact.
Fraction of upstream samples represented in the final integrated metadata table, calculated as a completeness measure for the derivative table. Typical values are between 0 and 1.
Fraction of expected metadata fields that remain missing across the integrated table, used as a table-quality indicator for the derivative artifact. Typical values are between 0 and 1.
Overall quality flag for the integrated metadata table, indicating whether the derivative artifact is complete and usable for downstream ecological analysis.
Fraction of the intended schema fields successfully populated in the integrated table, recorded as a derivative completeness metric for the final artifact.
Overall integrity score summarizing consistency of joins, field harmonization, and completeness in the integrated metadata table, measured after the table is built.

comparative_marine_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included downstream comparative-analysis parameters that describe how the integrated metadata, taxa profiles, and function profiles were contrasted across regions and gradients: grouping variables, statistical methods, covariates, and significance thresholds. I excluded the raw and derived input content itself because those belong to upstream derivative nodes, and I excluded final interpreted findings because those belong to the downstream marine_community_insights derivative. I also avoided duplicate field ids already used elsewhere in the DAG, especially generic count-style fields, and focused on the comparative workflow settings and output quality.

md_schema.descr: Date on which the comparative marine analysis was performed, recorded at the start or completion of the downstream comparative workflow.
Primary grouping variable used to compare diversity and functional potential across samples, such as ocean region, habitat type, or environmental gradient.
Name of the statistical test or modeling approach used to compare community diversity and functional potential across groups, such as ANOVA, PERMANOVA, linear models, or mixed-effects models.
Method used to control false discovery or adjust p-values across multiple comparisons in the downstream analysis, recorded as the correction applied to the comparative workflow.
Significance threshold used for hypothesis testing in the comparative analysis, typically a p-value cutoff such as 0.05.
Set of covariates included in the comparative analysis model, such as temperature, salinity, depth, or sample type, recorded as a summary descriptor of the adjustment variables.
Effect size metric used to summarize differences across marine regions or environmental gradients, such as beta coefficient, R-squared, or standardized difference.
Boolean indicator of whether the comparative analysis completed successfully and produced interpretable downstream comparison results.

marine_community_insights.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only the final interpreted comparison outputs: a result identifier, the output format, a compact summary of the analysis scope, and high-level result quality/completeness indicators. I excluded the underlying taxa/function profiles, statistical settings, and intermediate comparison parameters because those belong to upstream nodes, and I avoided duplicating generic count fields already used elsewhere in the DAG. The fields here are meant to describe the final insight artifact itself rather than the biological measurements or modeling inputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final marine community insights derivative, formatted as a result or report code such as 'INSIGHT_0001'. This identifies the summarized comparative output across marine microbiomes.
File or serialization format of the final insights artifact, such as PDF, HTML, JSON, TSV, or CSV, recorded as the output representation of the derivative result.
Short text description of the comparison scope summarized in the final insights artifact, such as the marine regions, environmental gradients, and community properties evaluated.
Number of major comparative findings, themes, or summary statements captured in the final insights output, counted after the analysis is complete.
Number of statistically supported diversity or functional patterns reported in the final derivative result, counted from the comparative analysis summary.
Overall confidence score for the final community insights output, reflecting the consistency and support of the comparative results. Use the project-defined scale if available, typically 0 to 1.
Boolean indicator of whether the final comparative insights artifact is complete and ready for downstream reporting or dissemination.
